title: Bulk change that succeeds shows how many parts were updated
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BOK-01) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.
  • Inventory part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BOK-02) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.
  • Inventory part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BOK-03) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.
  • {Part-A} and {Part-B} and {Part-C} share the start of their numbers (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BOK-0), so one search lists them together.
custom_steps:
1. On the Active tab search the shared start (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BOK-0), turn on "Deactivate parts", tick {Part-A} and {Part-B}, click "Deactivate" and confirm with "Deactivate".
  2. Read the message at the bottom right and wait 10 seconds.
  3. Turn on "Deactivate parts" again, tick {Part-C}, click "Deactivate" and confirm.
  4. Read the message.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: A green message reads "2 parts updated." and fades on its own; {Part-A} and {Part-B} have left the Active tab.
  • Step 4: A green message reads "1 part updated."; {Part-C} has left the Active tab.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S10-R12, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 4.5 (Done: "2 parts updated."), 13 Oct copy. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (Bulk change, every part changed): “"{n} parts updated." ("1 part updated." for one) | Success toast, fades on its own”
  • S10-R12: “After a bulk change, the system shows how many parts changed and how many failed.”
